one_line.text: American author who distils history into strategic guidance on power, seduction, war, and mastery, beginning with The 48 Laws of Power in 1998.

biography.text: Greene was born and raised in Los Angeles, studied at the University of California, Berkeley, and finished a degree in classical studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He estimates he worked around eighty jobs before writing books, including construction worker, translator, magazine editor and writer in New York (including Esquire), and Hollywood story developer. In 1995, while helping plan the Fabrica media school in Italy, he met the book packager Joost Elffers and pitched the idea that became The 48 Laws of Power, published by Viking in 1998. He has since written a string of international bestsellers including The Art of Seduction, The 33 Strategies of War, The 50th Law with the rapper 50 Cent, Mastery, The Laws of Human Nature, and The Daily Laws.

background.text: His classical-studies training and itinerant early career shaped a method he has kept across all his books: mining ancient and modern history for recurring patterns of behaviour and packaging them as numbered laws or strategies. The partnership with Elffers, a producer of highly designed books, also set the distinctive visual, aphoristic format of the early titles.

expertise.text: Greene's authority is as a synthesiser and storyteller of historical power dynamics, not as an academic historian or social scientist. His books rest on wide reading and pattern-finding across biography and history, presented with confident generalisation. None of the cited sources records formal training in history, psychology, or political science beyond his classical-studies degree.

perspective_and_limits.text: Greene writes deliberately amoral analysis: he describes how power has been taken and kept, not whether it should be. That stance produces unusually frank observation and also his work's main weaknesses, selection of colourful cases over systematic evidence, contradictions between laws, and little interest in cooperation, institutions, or the many settings where manipulation backfires. Readers get sharper eyes for status games; they must supply their own ethics and their own checks on generalisation.

selected_works.title: The 48 Laws of Power
selected_works.relationship: Debut and signature work: forty-eight historically illustrated laws of acquiring and defending power.

selected_works.title: The Art of Seduction
selected_works.relationship: Second book, applying the same historical-pattern method to seduction and persuasion.

selected_works.title: The 33 Strategies of War
selected_works.relationship: Military-strategy volume in the same numbered-laws format.

selected_works.title: Mastery
selected_works.relationship: A shift toward self-development: how masters across history acquired their craft.

selected_works.title: The Laws of Human Nature
selected_works.relationship: Later, more psychological treatment of the drives behind behaviour; catalogued separately in this library.
